title: Is knife hunting the fairest way to hunt?
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss whether knife hunting is the fairest way to hunt, drawing on the principle of fair chase, which calls for a balance between hunter and prey. They contrast tech-heavy hunting (scent-killing detergent, scopes, bait, feeders) with knife hunting, then cover internet hunting, a Texas website that let users fire a remote-controlled gun at animals and was shut down by lawmakers. They describe knife hunting for wild boar, which involves dogs flushing hogs from brush and the hunter leaping in to stab them, and mention a 1906 Florida hunt that used throwing knives. The episode closes with a "famous birthday" segment on Louise Joy Brown, the first baby conceived through in vitro fertilization, born in Manchester, England. Ad reads for Visa and the camera sponsor appear throughout. The episode includes a subliminal Russian language module joke.

segments.title: Opening banter and sponsor read
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the show, with a Visa sponsor read and a joke about a subliminal Russian language module. Josh introduces the topic of knife hunting and the article he wrote on it.

segments.title: Fair chase principle
segments.summary: Josh explains the principle of fair chase, which calls for a balance between hunter and prey. Chuck gives examples of high-tech hunting gear and scent-masking products that tilt the balance toward the hunter.

segments.title: Internet hunting
segments.summary: The hosts discuss a Texas website that let people remotely aim and fire a gun at animals through a camera feed. Lawmakers shut it down, and sportsmen's groups as well as animal rights advocates opposed it.

segments.title: Knife hunting wild boar
segments.summary: Knife hunting is described as dogs flushing wild hogs from brush, with the hunter leaping in to stab them. The hosts note that wild boar can weigh up to about 700 pounds and that an 1906 Florida hunter also used throwing knives. They mention a viral eleven-foot boar story that Snopes verified, which turned out to be a former pet.

segments.title: Visa sponsor read
segments.summary: Visa sponsor read about online fraud monitoring and purchase protection.

segments.title: Famous birthday: Louise Joy Brown
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh discuss Louise Joy Brown, born in Manchester, England, who was the first person conceived through in vitro fertilization. They explain the Latin meaning of in vitro and the term test tube baby.

segments.title: Sign-off and camera ad
segments.summary: Closing remarks invite listener feedback at the podcast email address, followed by a camera sponsor read.
